basics.name: Edgar Dolores-Tesillos
basics.summary: Atmospheric scientist with expertise in extratropical dynamics, blocking, and climate hazards. Experienced in analyzing high-impact weather events and assessing climate risk using large ensemble datasets and high-resolution simulations. Strong programming background (Python, Fortran) and high-performance computing skills. Passionate about applying science to real-world risk challenges.

education.summary: Thesis: Changes in Extratropical Cyclone Dynamics in the North Atlantic in a Warming Climate
Thesis: Detection of the impact of soil moisture on convective initiation in Mexico
Thesis: Characteristic thermodynamics profile for a Norte event in the port of Veracruz.

work.summary: Project: Representation and Impacts of Atmospheric Blocking in the nextGEMS
highlights: Assessed biases in blocking frequency, duration, and dynamics in high-resolution climate simulations (e.g., ICON, IFS)
Evaluated large-scale circulation patterns influencing renewable energy variability and extreme weather in Europe
Utilized diagnostic tools in Python and leveraged high-performance computing (DKRZ, Levante)
Engaged in interdisciplinary collaborations and workshops focused on climate hazard impacts

work.summary: Project: Extratropical Cyclone Dynamics in CESM Large Ensemble
highlights: Investigated shifts in cyclone tracks and changes in wind and precipitation extremes with direct implications for climate risk
Developed diagnostic, statistical, and visualization tools using Python and Fortran
Contributed to publications and presented findings at international conferences
